newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa says cost cuts boost competitiveness.
newsitem.headline: Dasa says cost cuts boost competitiveness.

text.p: Dasa, the aerospace unit of Daimler-Benz AG, said on Thursday its restructuring measures were paying off after massive losses last year, helping it to boost its competitiveness and win new orders.

Industry sources said that Dasa, which posted a net loss of 4.2 billion marks ($2.78 billion) last year, could even return to profit at the operating level in the second half of this year. A company spokesman declined to comment on the speculation.
In the first nine months of this year Dasa increased its incoming orders by 89 percent to 13.6 billion marks. Turnover rose by 18 percent to 8.3 billion marks, results announced by Daimler showed.

Those figures do not include U.S. Air's U.N. decision, announced on Wednesday to buy 120 Airbuses with a further option on 280 in a deal worth at least $5 billion. Dasa is a member of the four-nation Airbus consortium.

"The major order by USAir is ...proves our international competitiveness," chief executive Manfred Bischoff said in a statement. "It is a clear and renewed vote of confidence by a renowned airline in the quality of the Airbus family.

Dasa in August pushed through cost cuts at its Daimler-Benz Aerospace Airbus GmbH unit in Hamburg, completing a company-wide savings programme designed to make it profitable even if the dollar is weak.

Industry sources said that Dasa, which posted a net loss of 4.2 billion marks last year, could even return to profit at the operating level in the second half of this year. A company spokesman declined to comment on the speculation.
Dasa owns 37.9 percent of Airbus, the same size as the stake held by France's Aerospatiale. British Aerospace owns 20 percent and Spain's CASA 4.2 percent.
